scenes.headline: "Hi Mum, I lost my phone"
scenes.body: New number. Urgent bill. Probably a scam.
scenes.say: Parents: that Hi Mum, new number text may be a scam.

scenes.headline: First a chat, then a bill
scenes.body: They say they can't get into their online banking, so could you pay?
scenes.say: Scammers message you, often on WhatsApp, pretending to be your child on a new number. They chat first, then ask you to pay an urgent bill, saying they can't get into their online banking.

scenes.headline: Now they pose as a parent too
scenes.body: "Lost my bank card. Can you cover the bill?"
scenes.source: North Wales Police via Deeside.com, April 20
scenes.say: In April, North Wales Police warned of a twist: texts that pretend to come from a parent who lost their bank card, asking you to cover a bill.

scenes.headline: of these reports came from people over 55
scenes.say: In Australia in twenty twenty-two, eighty-two percent of these reports came from people over fifty-five.

scenes.headline: A new number proves nothing.
scenes.body: New number plus urgent money is the whole scam.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a new number proves nothing. A new number plus an urgent money request is the whole scam.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: Ask what only they would know
scenes.say: Tonight, tell your family: call the number already saved in your phone, ask something only they would know, and never send money until you're sure who gets it.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
